bug_description.original: OSS-Fuzz issue 42534761 (fwupd): Heap-buffer-overflow READ 4 found by fuzz target uswid_fuzzer [asan]. https://issues.oss-fuzz.com/issues/42534761
bug_description.original_source: sample_info.json issue_description / reproduction_report.json / sanitizer_trace.txt / default_crash_trace.txt / patch.diff / staged vulnerable source in `_work/src/fwupd` / staged `poc`
bug_description.normalized: Stage 01 reproduced `AddressSanitizer: heap-buffer-overflow READ of size 4` in `fu_coswid_firmware_write` while `uswid_fuzzer` processed the exact staged 38-byte witness with SHA-256 `cff11d72a4c21903c499157f62d19d42b9ae122d77d6c3911f9e77da060b4297`. In `fu_uswid_firmware_parse()`, the uncompressed wrapper path materializes the remaining 15 bytes of that witness into `payload`, records their actual length as 15, and slices them with `fu_bytes_new_offset()` into `fw2` for the inner coSWID parser. `fu_coswid_firmware_parse()` rereads those bytes, and `cbor_load()` decodes `bf02bf18219f090101020104ffffff` as the CBOR map `{2:{33:[9,1,1,2,1,4]}}`, where tag 2 is `ENTITY` and tag 33 is `ROLE`. `fu_coswid_firmware_parse_entity()` then allocates a zeroed 40-byte `FuCoswidFirmwareEntity`; its `roles[6]` array starts as six `FU_COSWID_ENTITY_ROLE_UNKNOWN` sentinels. The ROLE array length is exactly 6, but the only capacity guard rejects counts already `>= 6`, so the parser stores all six nonzero integers `[9,1,1,2,1,4]` into `roles[0..5]` and leaves no in-bounds zero terminator. That entity is retained in `priv->entities`, and the later reserialization path `fu_uswid_firmware_write -> fu_firmware_write -> fu_coswid_firmware_write` scans `entity->roles` until it sees `FU_COSWID_ENTITY_ROLE_UNKNOWN`. Because slots 0 through 5 are all nonzero, the loop condition at line 811 evaluates `entity->roles[6]` and ASan reports the saved 4-byte heap-buffer-overflow read 0 bytes past the 40-byte allocation created at parse line 412. The staged patch resolves this by replacing the sentinel-terminated array with a bitfield and rejecting invalid role values before recording them.

source.code: payload = fu_input_stream_read_bytes(stream, offset + hdrsz, payloadsz, error);
source.description: Source. This is the first project statement on the vulnerable path that materializes the attacker-controlled embedded coSWID payload from the uSWID wrapper into project state.
source.value_from: The staged 38-byte `gt_results/arvo_42534761/poc` has SHA-256 `cff11d72a4c21903c499157f62d19d42b9ae122d77d6c3911f9e77da060b4297`. `fu_input_stream_read_bytes()` may return fewer bytes than requested, and on this witness this call returns the remaining 15 bytes `bf02bf18219f090101020104ffffff` into `payload`.
source.note: The wrapper has already parsed `hdrsz` and selected the `FU_USWID_PAYLOAD_COMPRESSION_NONE` branch, so the vulnerable inner payload first becomes a project `GBytes` here rather than inside `fu_coswid_firmware_parse()`.

root_cause.description: Root cause. On the witnessed sixth loop iteration, this store writes the last attacker-controlled nonzero role into `roles[5]`. Together with the earlier five nonzero stores, that exhausts the six-slot sentinel-terminated array and leaves no in-bounds `FU_COSWID_ENTITY_ROLE_UNKNOWN` entry for the later write-side scan. The patch fixes this by switching to a bitfield and rejecting invalid role values before setting it.
root_cause.note: The immediately preceding guard at line 428 only rejects `entity_role_cnt >= G_N_ELEMENTS(entity->roles)`, so the exact six-element witness `[9,1,1,2,1,4]` is fully stored instead of preserving a zero terminator.

sink.description: Project-side sink. Evaluating this loop condition on the stored six-value role array reads `entity->roles[6]` past the 40-byte `FuCoswidFirmwareEntity` allocation.
sink.note: ASan frame 0 names this exact line in `fu_coswid_firmware_write`; the reported address is 0 bytes to the right of the 40-byte region allocated at parse line 412.

parser_admitted.description: After slicing `fw2` from the wrapper payload, the outer uSWID parser invokes the inner coSWID parser on that exact byte range.

tainted_value_origin.description: This loop turns the decoded attacker-controlled `ROLE` field into the vulnerability-relevant six-element array that feeds the fixed `roles[6]` buffer. For the witness, `pairs[i].value` is `[9,1,1,2,1,4]`.
tainted_value_origin.value_from: The staged payload `bf02bf18219f090101020104ffffff` decodes to `{2: {33: [9,1,1,2,1,4]}}`, where tag 2 is `ENTITY` and tag 33 is `ROLE`.
tainted_value_origin.note: The array length matches `G_N_ELEMENTS(entity->roles)` exactly, and every parsed integer is nonzero, so consuming all six elements exhausts the sentinel-terminated representation.

coarse_trace.summary: The outer uSWID parser reads the embedded coSWID bytes into `payload`, records that the actual returned payload length is 15, and slices `fw2` for the inner parser.
The inner parser rereads `fw2` and `cbor_load()` materializes the root CBOR map `{ENTITY:{ROLE:[9,1,1,2,1,4]}}`, which reaches `fu_coswid_firmware_parse_entity()`.

The entity parser allocates a zeroed 40-byte `FuCoswidFirmwareEntity`, accepts all six nonzero ROLE integers because the guard only rejects counts already `>= 6`, and stores the resulting unterminated role array in `priv->entities`.
Later reserialization reuses that same entity object, and the unbounded sentinel scan over `entity->roles` reads past `roles[5]` at line 811.

fine_trace.code: payload = fu_input_stream_read_bytes(stream, offset + hdrsz, payloadsz, error);
fine_trace.note: Source step. In the uncompressed wrapper path, this call materializes the remaining 15 witness bytes `bf02bf18219f090101020104ffffff` into `payload`; `fu_input_stream_read_bytes()` may return fewer bytes than the requested `payloadsz`.
The outer parser normalizes the actual returned payload length to 15, and that concrete size is what the later slice operation uses.

fine_trace.code: fw2 = fu_bytes_new_offset(payload, offset_tmp, payloadsz - offset_tmp, error);
fine_trace.note: With `offset_tmp` at 0 on the first and only loop iteration, `fw2` aliases the full 15-byte coSWID payload and becomes the object passed to `fu_firmware_parse()`.
Inside `fu_coswid_firmware_parse()`, the inner parser rereads all bytes from `fw2` into local `fw`, carrying the same 15-byte payload forward.
The 15-byte payload is materialized as the CBOR map `{2:{33:[9,1,1,2,1,4]}}`. Root tag 2 (`ENTITY`) is the only top-level tag, so parsing proceeds into `fu_coswid_firmware_parse_entity()`.
parse_entity allocates a 40-byte `FuCoswidFirmwareEntity` with `g_new0`, so `entity->roles[0..5]` start as six `FU_COSWID_ENTITY_ROLE_UNKNOWN` zero sentinels.
For tag 33 (`ROLE`), `pairs[i].value` is the six-element array `[9,1,1,2,1,4]`. `cbor_array_size(pairs[i].value)` is 6, exactly matching the six-slot `roles` buffer, and every element is nonzero.

Before each array write, the only capacity guard is `entity_role_cnt >= G_N_ELEMENTS(entity->roles)`. It stays false on iterations 0 through 5, including the final write into `roles[5]`, and therefore does not reserve room for a zero terminator.

On the sixth iteration, this store writes the last nonzero role `4` into `entity->roles[5]`; together with the earlier stores `9,1,1,2,1`, the in-bounds buffer becomes `[9,1,1,2,1,4]` with no remaining `FU_COSWID_ENTITY_ROLE_UNKNOWN` sentinel.
The entity carrying the fully nonzero `roles[0..5]` buffer is retained in `priv->entities`, so the later serialization path reuses this same heap object.
During reserialization, `fu_coswid_firmware_write()` retrieves that stored entity back from `priv->entities` into local `entity`.
Sink step. The loop condition itself reads `entity->roles[j]`; because slots 0 through 5 are all nonzero, the evaluation for `j == 6` performs the saved 4-byte read just past the 40-byte allocation.

cross_validation.sink_matches_crash: Yes. ASan frame 0 is `fu_coswid_firmware_write` at `libfwupdplugin/fu-coswid-firmware.c:811`, the same fine-trace sink that evaluates `entity->roles[j]` and reads past the allocation.
cross_validation.root_cause_matches_allocation_context: Yes at object level. The allocation context is `g_new0` at `fu_coswid_firmware_parse_entity` line 412, and the fine trace shows that same 40-byte object's `roles[6]` field sequence being fully filled with nonzero values before the sink scans past it.

poc.trigger: Stage 01's saved vulnerable run fed the staged 38-byte witness to `uswid_fuzzer`; its trailing coSWID payload decodes to `{2:{33:[9,1,1,2,1,4]}}`, so `fu_coswid_firmware_parse_entity()` fills all six `entity->roles` slots with nonzero values and the later write loop at line 811 reads `entity->roles[6]` past the allocation.

format.name: uSWID container with embedded coSWID CBOR payload
format.contract: The witnessed trigger is the exact 38-byte file whose first 23 bytes are `53424f4dd6ba2eaca3e67a52aaee3baf01170020202020` and whose trailing 15-byte coSWID payload is `bf02bf18219f090101020104ffffff`. That payload decodes to `{2:{33:[9,1,1,2,1,4]}}` (`ENTITY` -> `ROLE`). This exact six-element nonzero role array is parsed into `entity->roles[0..5]` without leaving an in-bounds `FU_COSWID_ENTITY_ROLE_UNKNOWN` sentinel, which is why the later writer condition `entity->roles[j] != FU_COSWID_ENTITY_ROLE_UNKNOWN` evaluates `entity->roles[6]` out of bounds.
